problem: The website browser lane accepted a Netlify deploy-preview after targeted route readiness, then reused that preview for a full sitemap visibility sweep. Unrelated preview routes returned HTTP 403 and were misclassified as public-page visibility regressions.
root_cause: Preview readiness proved only targeted affected routes, not public reachability of every sitemap route.
Broad visibility/header/browser checks reused the preview base URL instead of the exact local candidate.
Provider access status and visual regression evidence were conflated.
prevention: Use Netlify deploy-preview only for targeted routes that were positively proven route-ready.
Always build and serve the exact local candidate for broad/full-site browser checks.
Run full sitemap visibility, header/menu and broad high-risk browser checks against http://127.0.0.1:4173.
Treat preview HTTP 403 as provider/access evidence, never as a UI/layout failure.
